D.t: Mark Warner leads by 16.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 600,566 votes; a one point swing is about 18,547 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +9.1 and D +23.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Fairfax County, a projected net 236,082 votes; Arlington County, a projected net 74,623 votes; Richmond city, a projected net 73,168 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

The large counties within 12 points: Virginia Beach city, D +10.9, 5.2% of the vote; Stafford County, D +9.8, 1.8% of the vote; Spotsylvania County, R +1.2, 1.7% of the vote; James City County, D +12.0, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Mark Warner runs furthest behind in Hanover County, Bedford County, Frederick County. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 71% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.56 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 56 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.29 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 59 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Mark Warner: Immigration voters 22 to 75, Small counties 40 to 57, White voters 49 to 48. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$7.5M cash against $230K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Activity: $2K in Google political ads this cycle.
